A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same recurrent natural actor-critic work for POMDPs. Their main text, equations, figures, references and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Appendix C reports original Rec-TD simulations on a random POMDP with 8 states, 8 observations and 4 actions. Figures 2–3 show learning errors and parameter deviations.

after.justification: Appendix C reports revised original Rec-TD simulations. Figures 2–4 present learning errors, parameter deviations and sequence-length sensitivity.

M1.justification: The diagonal RNN architecture, renamed IndRNN, and basic actor-critic construction remain. However, v2 Algorithm 2 omits the network-gradient factor from the TD update, and Section 6.1 replaces the zero-centered actor-direction constraint with initialization-centered Omega. Appendices B and E retain the former formulations, leaving actual procedural changes versus transcription errors unresolved.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate policy prediction on the same type of randomly generated finite POMDP, with short- and long-memory greedy policies. Changed exploration probabilities and sequence lengths refine these retained scenarios. POPGym and other newly discussed work are not evaluated benchmarks.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically compares Rec-TD against another algorithm. Figures compare network widths and sequence lengths; newly discussed memoryless TD, transformers and other recurrent architectures are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix C substantially revises the experimental design. Example 1 changes the discount from 0.7 to 0.9, and Example 2 changes exploration probability from 0.3 to 0.25. The earlier T=8/32 studies become T=8 width comparisons plus a separate m=256, T=8/16/24 study, with revised iteration ranges.

E4.justification: Width and memory-length sensitivity already appear in v1. v2 removes the short-memory T=32 comparison, revises the long-memory horizon sweep, and adds input-weight deviations to the long-memory diagnostics. These are refinements of existing sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report five trials and 90% confidence intervals for MSTD. In v1, parameter-deviation bands describe variation across neurons within one trial; v2 captions attribute the curves and intervals to five trials. The statistical basis of those bands changes without a reported increase in trial count.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 replace the principal loss and parameter-deviation curves under revised settings, removing the previous T=32 results and adding long-memory input-weight results. New Figure 4 reports higher MSTD for T=24 than T=16 than T=8 at m=256. Larger-width benefits persist, but the replaced curves do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorem 7.3 becomes Theorem 6.3 with a materially altered bound: the explicit sqrt(N)/sqrt(m) contribution disappears, although Appendix E retains the drift argument producing it. v2 also states a misspecification-error extension, broadens the transportation-map definition to joint parameter dependence, and removes the linear-transportation special case from v1 Remark 7.9. These change formal content beyond notation.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains finite-time analysis of recurrent TD and natural policy gradient, including long-memory difficulties. v2 explicitly qualifies abstract-level optimality by function approximation and adds perceptual-aliasing resolution and stabilizing regularization to the introduction's stated contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussion: why diagonal recurrence matters, why independent trajectory restarts are needed, what happens without realizability, and how concentrability relates to exploration. The conclusion replaces LSTM/GRU and attention directions with input normalization and preconditioning while describing long-memory limitations more precisely through resource requirements.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents shared random samples and network initialization between the two experimental examples, spells out trajectory sampling in pseudocode, and specifies critic/SGD learning-rate scalings. Symmetric initialization and max-norm projection were already documented in v1 Appendix A; their move into the main text is not new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The architecture is repositioned through IndRNN references by Li et al. and practical work including POPGym, Ni et al. and Lu et al. Related work adds substantive contrasts with Guo et al.'s linear POMDPs and Uehara et al.'s structured models, replacing much of the earlier diagonal-linear-network and generic RNN motivation. Publication updates to retained Cayci references alone are not counted.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around two observations and three research questions. v2 expands the function-class explanation, incorporates initialization and projection into Section 3, presents algorithms as pseudocode, and moves references before the appendices. Terminology shifts from diagonal Elman-type RNNs to IndRNNs throughout.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography, headings, author presentation and page headers, and adds two algorithm boxes. Figures 2–3 are reorganized from multirow displays into three-panel rows with revised axes and captions; Figure 4 adds a separate horizon comparison. Figure 1 is restyled and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 improves exposition, explains assumptions and limitations more fully, and makes the experimental comparison clearer through a common discount and documented shared samples and initialization. However, its TD pseudocode omits a gradient factor, its actor constraint conflicts with the appendix proofs, and its main NPG bound drops an iteration-dependent term without a corresponding derivation. These affect reproducibility and the central theoretical guarantee, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
